inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,708 normalized lines of the 70-page OCR. The recoverable prose supplies a dense conceptual arc from semiclassical correspondence and spectral statistics through arithmetic correspondences, quantum limits, eigenfunction norms, L-function bridges, and trace/pretrace proof mechanisms. Thirty-seven units retain those mechanisms; figure-only regions, the raw eigenvalue table, acknowledgements, and references are accounted for without promotion. Formula-bearing claims are accepted only where surrounding prose fixes their role, with scan verification explicitly retained because the assignment labels the extraction lower-confidence OCR.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Title, date, and author metadata only.

sections_inspected.label: Section 1. Background
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Sets the semiclassical geodesic model, contrasts integrable localization with chaotic quantum limits, and introduces random-wave and spectral-statistics diagnostics.

sections_inspected.label: Section 2.1. The Stadium
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses a chaotic billiard with bouncing-ball families to distinguish finite-energy visual scarring from persistent strong scarring.

sections_inspected.label: Section 2.2. Hyperbolic Surfaces
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces hyperbolic quotient models and numerical evidence for Gaussian, nonlocalized eigenfunctions on compact and modular examples.

sections_inspected.label: Section 2.3. Fine structure of the spectrum
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares simplicity and number variance across integrable, nonarithmetic chaotic, and arithmetic chaotic spectra, including the arithmetic trace criterion.

sections_inspected.label: Section 3. Arithmetic Manifolds
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops length-spectrum multiplicity, Hecke correspondences, scarring and norm conjectures, exceptional theta lifts, cusp-form deformation, and the shifted role of random-matrix ideas.

sections_inspected.label: Section 4. L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the zeta/general-L-function framework and connects sup norms and equidistribution to central values, Rankin-Selberg products, Lindelof bounds, and subconvexity.

sections_inspected.label: Section 5. Outline of some proofs
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Exhibits trace-formula, bounded-clustering, Hecke-separation, pretrace-amplification, and CM-point mechanisms behind the earlier results.

sections_inspected.label: Section 6. Conclusion and acknowledgements
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recapitulates the represented mechanisms and records author acknowledgements.

sections_inspected.label: References
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic apparatus; inspected for boundary completeness but not semantic-unit content.

accepted_units.title: Semiclassical geodesic dictionary
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies quantum chaos as the semiclassical study of a quantized chaotic Hamiltonian and, for geodesic flow, turns the limit of Planck scale into the high-Laplacian-eigenvalue limit. This is the source's governing representation change between dynamics and spectral geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Hamiltonian, Laplace-Beltrami quantization, stationary states, and the correspondence question; lines 11-25 supply only lecture-level motivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core meaning is recoverable from prose; displayed metric and operator formulas are OCR-degraded and should be checked against the scan before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Integrable torus quantization produces localized quasimodes
accepted_units.why_material: Explains how invariant tori yield quantization conditions and quasimodes localized on the torus, then makes the mechanism geometric through the whispering-gallery example. It gives the comparison class against which chaotic localization is judged.
accepted_units.context_note: The ellipse example supplies the invariant-caustic picture and physical projection of phase-space localization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual chain is prose-safe; the Bohr-Sommerfeld and action-variable formulas and figure details require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Stable periodic orbits organize spectrum; unstable ones pose the chaos problem
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts the failure of integrable quantization in chaotic negative curvature with the strong spectral and quasimode influence of a stable closed geodesic. The unresolved influence of unstable periodic orbits is isolated as a central quantum-chaos obstruction.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the stable-orbit theorem, its Weyl-law scale, and singular limiting measure, which together make the contrast operational rather than rhetorical.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The stable-versus-unstable conclusion is clear in prose; theorem asymptotics and constants are formula-sensitive OCR.

accepted_units.title: Quantum ergodicity constrains most states but leaves exceptional quantum limits
accepted_units.why_material: Defines eigenfunction probability measures and quantum limits, states full-density equidistribution, and records geodesic-flow invariance of any limit. It sharply separates an almost-everywhere theorem from the unresolved possibility of exceptional localization or scarring.
accepted_units.context_note: The phase-space strengthening and examples of invariant singular measures are needed to understand what quantum ergodicity does not exclude.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The measure-theoretic content is recoverable from prose; notation in the displayed convergence and projection identity should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Random-wave behavior yields Gaussian and extreme-value diagnostics
accepted_units.why_material: Turns the random-wave proposal for individual chaotic eigenfunctions into falsifiable distributional and sup-norm expectations rather than leaving it as a visual analogy.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit follows the exceptional-limit gap and motivates the later numerical and norm investigations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Gaussian prediction is prose-safe; the iterated-logarithm-style displayed asymptotic is OCR-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Number variance separates Poisson from random-matrix rigidity
accepted_units.why_material: Defines a local spectral statistic and compares its scale under Poisson, Gaussian orthogonal, and Gaussian unitary models. It supplies the quantitative language of clustering versus rigidity used throughout the source.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes rescaling to unit mean spacing, ensemble invariance, and the contrast between linear and logarithmic growth of variance.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Model roles and growth contrast are clear; exact normalizations, ensemble density, and asymptotic constants require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Universal statistics have a finite spectral window
accepted_units.why_material: Records the integrable-Poisson and chaotic-GOE heuristic only within a universal range, beyond which system-specific periodic-orbit oscillations take over. This guards against treating random-matrix behavior as scale-free.
accepted_units.context_note: The source assumes two dimensions for the stated crossover scale and flags analogous rigidity conjectures.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The scale distinction is prose-safe; the exact OCR rendering of the upper crossover scale should be verified.

accepted_units.title: Stadium dynamics separates visual scars from persistent strong scarring
accepted_units.why_material: The stadium combines global ergodicity with measure-zero bouncing-ball families that influence the spectrum. The source then distinguishes finite-energy enhancement near unstable orbits from strong scarring defined through singular support of a limiting measure.
accepted_units.context_note: The boundary extension of quantum ergodicity makes clear that exceptional-looking modes coexist with almost-all equidistribution.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Definitions and distinctions are prose-recoverable; visual claims depend on omitted figures and should not be used without the scan.

accepted_units.title: Hyperbolic quotients provide controlled chaotic models
accepted_units.why_material: Realizes constant-negative-curvature systems as discrete-group quotients in upper-half-plane or disk models and introduces compact/orbifold and Hecke-triangle examples. This is the geometric substrate for the later arithmetic/nonarithmetic comparison.
accepted_units.context_note: The fundamental-domain descriptions are enough for role identification; the figures are not needed for the abstract quotient construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Quotient meaning is prose-safe; group generators, angle notation, and figure geometry are OCR/scan dependent.

accepted_units.title: Compact and modular hyperbolic spectra test the random-wave picture
accepted_units.why_material: Reports nonlocalized, approximately Gaussian eigenstates on a compact hyperbolic surface, then distinguishes the modular surface's continuous Eisenstein spectrum from its embedded discrete cusp forms. The same chaotic geometry thus supports different spectral representations that must not be conflated.
accepted_units.context_note: Figure evidence is summarized only at the level asserted by the checked prose; modular cusp-form plots continue after an extraction-heavy interval.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Qualitative conclusions are prose-grounded; plots and numerical thresholds require original-scan inspection.

accepted_units.title: Modular cusp forms motivate a Gaussian distribution conjecture
accepted_units.why_material: Converts repeated numerical observations of no localization and Gaussian amplitude behavior into a limiting distribution conjecture for modular eigenfunctions.
accepted_units.context_note: This is computational and heuristic evidence, not an independent proof of random-wave behavior.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conjectural Gaussian claim is clear; its OCR-rendered normalization parameter should be verified against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Simplicity and number variance test distinct spectral features
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the conjectural simplicity of the modular spectrum from number-variance comparisons: an integrable billiard follows Poisson while the chaotic stadium follows GOE in the universal range, with bouncing-ball effects predicted later.
accepted_units.context_note: The modular simplicity observation becomes an assumption in a later bound-state result; the variance comparison is a control, not evidence about arithmetic surfaces yet.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose claims are recoverable; exact computed eigenvalues and plotted curves are not included in the unit.

accepted_units.title: Arithmeticity is encoded by trace fields and bounded conjugates
accepted_units.why_material: Presents Takeuchi's trace-based characterization of arithmetic lattices and a stronger condition for quaternion-algebra origin, then classifies the arithmetic Hecke triangles. It recasts a geometric group property into algebraic data used later for spectral clustering.
accepted_units.context_note: The quaternion-group example begins the concrete realization but its formula is secondary to the criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Criterion clauses are prose-recoverable; set notation and the quaternion formula are degraded and need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Arithmetic chaos violates the naive GOE universality rule
accepted_units.why_material: Numerical number variance is Poisson-like for arithmetic hyperbolic triangles but GOE-like for nonarithmetic ones, despite both being chaotic. This is the source's central counterexample to identifying classical chaos with one universal spectral ensemble.
accepted_units.context_note: The summary also notes that eigenfunction random-wave behavior appears in both classes, separating eigenvalue and eigenfunction phenomena.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The comparison is explicit in prose; the plotted variance curves and precise numerical range require the scan.

accepted_units.title: Families of periodic trajectories force long-range spectral nonrigidity
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why a measure-zero positive-dimensional family of equal-period trajectories can force a variance lower bound outside the GOE window. The stadium, Sinai billiard, and integrable examples connect the trace mechanism to concrete systems.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposition is stated for closed manifolds while the stadium application is explicitly analogical and later noted as confirmed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mechanism and hypotheses are prose-safe; the exact averaged counting formula and lower-bound exponent are OCR-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Length multiplicity and bounded clustering drive arithmetic nonrigidity
accepted_units.why_material: States arithmetic number-variance lower bounds and identifies high multiplicity of the length spectrum, compressed into a bounded-clustering property of traces, as their cause. It also records the important asymmetry that useful lower bounds exist while upper bounds remain unavailable.
accepted_units.context_note: The quaternion-algebra case gains a stronger range because its spacing structure is easier to exploit than bounded clustering alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Causal interpretation is prose-grounded; theorem ranges, exponents, and displayed B-C cardinality need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Arithmetic manifolds carry nonlocal correspondences
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs arithmetic hyperbolic three-manifolds from quadratic forms, then abstracts a correspondence as a multivalued local-isometry relation and associates a Laplacian-commuting operator. Margulis's commensurator dichotomy makes an infinite correspondence family equivalent to arithmeticity.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the nonlocal structure that later bypasses spectral averaging barriers and separates singular supports.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The construction and equivalence are prose-recoverable; quadratic-form example, cosets, and operator normalization require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A commuting self-adjoint Hecke algebra refines Laplace eigenstates
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how classical and quaternionic correspondences form commuting self-adjoint Hecke operators, allowing simultaneous eigenbases. This extra spectral labeling is the arithmetic resource used to study individual eigenfunctions.
accepted_units.context_note: The text notes that simplicity would make the Hecke-basis condition automatic, but retains it as an explicit assumption.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Operator-algebra role is clear; explicit Hecke sums, multiplication law, and quaternion norm formulas are OCR-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Hecke structure rules out geodesic strong scars and motivates QUE
accepted_units.why_material: States that quantum limits for congruence arithmetic manifolds cannot have singular support confined to proper geodesic submanifolds, then formulates individual equidistribution as quantum unique ergodicity. It also highlights the counterfactual contrast: quantum uniqueness is expected although chaotic classical flow has many invariant measures.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is conditional on congruence/Hecke structure; the broader negative-curvature conjecture is not claimed as proved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The support and equidistribution statements are prose-safe; quantitative rate notation at line 1418 should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Local eigenfunction bounds are too geometry-blind for quantum chaos
accepted_units.why_material: Defines extremal eigenfunction norms, contrasts general local bounds with improved torus behavior, and ties that improvement to absolute continuity of quantum limits. The discussion isolates the need for global geometry or arithmetic to improve on local restriction-theoretic barriers.
accepted_units.context_note: Multiplicity complicates even integrable tori, preventing a simplistic integrable-versus-chaotic norm dichotomy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Comparative message is prose-grounded; piecewise exponents and individual norm inequalities require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The chaotic sup-norm conjecture links random waves to Lindelof
accepted_units.why_material: Formulates subpolynomial sup-norm growth for negatively curved surfaces, derives it heuristically from random waves, and identifies it as an eigenfunction analogue of Ramanujan whose arithmetic cases would imply Lindelof-type bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: The analogy to Sato-Tate is separately assigned to the Gaussian distribution conjecture; neither analogy is proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conceptual correspondences are clear; the exact exponent in the conjectured bound is OCR-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Hecke amplification beats the local sup-norm barrier
accepted_units.why_material: Records an arithmetic improvement over the general convexity-like sup-norm bound and a lower-growth result showing eigenfunctions are not uniformly bounded. Weighted Hecke spectral sums access individual states and reveal large values at a dense set of CM points.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly contrasts arithmetic amplification with the still-missing use of chaotic dynamics as a global ingredient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Method and qualitative consequences are prose-safe; theorem exponents and constants require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Sup-norm control would constrain spectral multiplicity
accepted_units.why_material: Derives an inequality from eigenvalue multiplicity to extremal sup norm, so the chaotic norm conjecture would imply subpolynomial multiplicity. The gap between this and known bounds exposes a major bottleneck despite numerical simplicity.
accepted_units.context_note: Applies beyond a chosen Hecke basis and therefore distinguishes basis-dependent amplification from eigenspace multiplicity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Logical implication is prose-recoverable; displayed inequalities and powers need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Theta lifts delimit random-wave universality in dimension three
accepted_units.why_material: An infinite subsequence of arithmetic three-dimensional eigenfunctions violates random-wave norm expectations. A special-point vanishing law explains the mechanism: most states vanish there, forcing the surviving states to be exceptionally large.
accepted_units.context_note: The source flags the open problem of finding a geometric rather than purely arithmetic explanation in a chaotic system without caustics or focusing.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Counterexample and vanishing mechanism are prose-safe; norm ranges, counting asymptotics, and the special quadratic-form coordinates require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Special L-values govern dissolution of cusp forms under deformation
accepted_units.why_material: Connects persistence of bound states on noncompact hyperbolic surfaces to arithmeticity and explains generic dissolution through nonvanishing Rankin-Selberg values, interpreted as a Fermi-golden-rule condition. A conditional finiteness theorem exposes spectral simplicity/multiplicity as the controlling unresolved input.
accepted_units.context_note: Numerical absence for nonarithmetic Hecke triangles is evidence only up to the tested range; arithmetic abundance is a separate theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mechanism and conditional structure are prose-recoverable; group matrices and exact spectral cutoffs should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Random-matrix ideas move from Laplace spectra to Hecke spectra
accepted_units.why_material: Reverses the failed random-matrix model for arithmetic Laplace eigenvalues by applying it to Hecke operators, relating semicircle and expansion behavior to Sato-Tate and Ramanujan conjectures and then to explicit pseudorandom graphs.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a transfer of modeling philosophy across operators, not a claim that the two spectra share statistics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual transfer is fully prose-based.

accepted_units.title: Zeta growth organizes RH, Lindelof, convexity, and subconvexity
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the Euler product, functional equation, RH, and Lindelof growth on the critical line, then distinguishes convexity from genuine improvements. This establishes the analytic hierarchy later mirrored by eigenfunction bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: The source notes RH implies Lindelof through a convexity argument for the logarithm but does not reverse that implication.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Hierarchy is prose-safe; formulas, historical exponents, and gamma normalization require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: General L-functions expose several convexity aspects
accepted_units.why_material: Abstracts degree, Euler product, analytic continuation, and functional equation into a general L-function template, then distinguishes spectral-height, conductor, and archimedean-parameter aspects of Lindelof and convexity. It provides the common language for the later bridges.
accepted_units.context_note: The countability/automorphy remark is exploratory context, while the bound hierarchy is the reusable mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Axiomatic roles are prose-recoverable; local Euler factors, gamma factors, and all aspect exponents need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Eisenstein series realize the continuous spectrum beside Hecke cusp forms
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs Eisenstein Laplace eigenfunctions, uses their Fourier expansion to identify near-square-integrability on the critical line, and decomposes the modular spectrum into continuous Eisenstein and discrete cuspidal parts. Both families can then test the same eigenfunction conjectures.
accepted_units.context_note: The Hecke eigenbasis for cusp forms is carried forward from the arithmetic-operator discussion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Spectral roles and decomposition are prose-safe; Fourier coefficients, Bessel function, and normalization identities are formula-sensitive OCR.

accepted_units.title: CM evaluation converts an Eisenstein sup norm into an L-value problem
accepted_units.why_material: Handles non-square-integrability by truncating Eisenstein series on a compact region, then evaluates at a CM point to factor the value through a quadratic-field zeta function. The eigenfunction sup-norm conjecture therefore implies a Lindelof bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit distinguishes local normalization from global L2 normalization and notes that other CM points extend the implication to imaginary quadratic fields and zeta itself.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Bridge is explicit in prose; truncation definition, Maass-Selberg norm identity, factorization, and exponents require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Cusp-form values at CM points encode twisted central L-values
accepted_units.why_material: Combines Hecke Euler products, a special-value identity, half-integral-weight correspondence, and central-value formulas to equate pointwise eigenfunction control at a CM point with Lindelof in the spectral-parameter aspect.
accepted_units.context_note: The equivalence depends on auxiliary coefficient bounds cited in the source and is specific to the stated modular Hecke-Maass setting.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conceptual dictionary is prose-grounded; every displayed identity and normalization is formula-heavy OCR and must be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Rankin-Selberg subconvexity is the threshold for individual equidistribution
accepted_units.why_material: Associates a degree-four Rankin-Selberg L-function to pairs of cusp forms, uses its integral representation to translate Lindelof-type control into decay of eigenfunction observables, and contrasts individual, mean, and quantum-ergodic estimates. Beating convexity in the spectral aspect is isolated as sufficient for individual equidistribution against the continuous spectrum.
accepted_units.context_note: The source expects the same behavior against cusp-form tests without claiming a direct L-function identity, and credits Hecke/Kuznetsov structure for the proved mean result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Threshold and comparison are prose-safe; integral representations, gamma factors, mean estimates, and exact powers require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Trace singularities turn periodic families into counting variance
accepted_units.why_material: Outlines how a clean positive-dimensional fixed set of the geodesic flow creates a trace-formula singularity, which a calculus lemma converts into an averaged lower bound for the Weyl counting remainder and hence number variance.
accepted_units.context_note: The nonzero leading coefficient and clean-intersection hypotheses are essential and are not automatic for every periodic family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Proof architecture is recoverable; distributional trace expansions and exponent arithmetic are severely OCR-sensitive and need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Bounded trace clustering makes Selberg smoothing yield arithmetic variance lower bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the Selberg trace formula to approximate a strongly smoothed spectral counting fluctuation by a length-side Dirichlet polynomial. Arithmetic spacing or bounded clustering controls its mean square and diagonal contribution, while off-diagonal ignorance blocks both the nonarithmetic analogue and useful upper bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly identifies smoothing as both enabling the lower-bound method and preventing direct control of unsmoothed variance.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mechanism, diagonal/off-diagonal distinction, and limitation are prose-safe; trace formula, Hilbert inequality lemma, and multiplicity sums require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A Hecke correspondence separates singular support and forbids geodesic scars
accepted_units.why_material: A separation lemma chooses a correspondence whose inverse image meets a proposed geodesic singular support in exactly one point. Applying the Hecke eigenrelation and Cauchy inequality to shrinking neighborhoods forces zero mass at that support point, contradicting singular support.
accepted_units.context_note: The algebraic separation lemma is cited rather than proved and depends on arithmetic representation theory; the analytic contradiction is outlined locally.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Logical proof route is prose-recoverable; neighborhood maps, eigenvalue inequality, and integral estimates require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Hecke amplification breaks the local pretrace barrier
accepted_units.why_material: The pretrace formula gives the local sup-norm bound from a unit-width spectral window; shortening the window makes the geometric side exponentially nonlocal. Applying Hecke operators and counting near-return correspondences creates weighted inequalities that can isolate an individual eigenfunction and beat that barrier.
accepted_units.context_note: The final amplifier weights cannot be chosen naively because a needed lower bound for Hecke coefficients is unavailable; the source records that a more careful choice resolves this.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Barrier and amplifier design are prose-safe; transforms, kernels, lattice counts, and weighted inequality require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: CM fixed points create an arithmetic resonance for large eigenfunctions
accepted_units.why_material: Chooses a point fixed by many Hecke correspondences so the geometric side receives an enhanced contribution for selected arithmetic indices. Comparing that enhancement with a general upper bound forces large values of some eigenfunctions at CM points.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the proof-side explanation of the lower bound and dense arithmetic enhancement stated earlier, not evidence of singular quantum limits.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Resonance mechanism is prose-grounded; transform positivity, prime splitting condition, and quantitative bounds require scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmetic chaos splits eigenvalue and eigenfunction universality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Arithmetic surfaces can display random-wave-like eigenfunctions while their Laplace eigenvalues are Poisson-like rather than GOE; arithmetic length multiplicities explain the spectral exception, and random-matrix structure reappears for Hecke operators.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The eigenfunction side is partly numerical/conjectural and the claims are dimension- and operator-specific.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Quantum unique ergodicity as a correspondence-to-subconvexity program
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The progression from full-density quantum ergodicity to exclusion of geodesic singular supports and finally individual equidistribution uses two complementary arithmetic routes: nonlocal correspondence separation and subconvex control of Rankin-Selberg periods.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The no-scarring theorem is restricted to Hecke arithmetic settings, while full QUE remains conjectural in this source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Hecke correspondences are both separators and amplifiers
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same nonlocal arithmetic correspondences refine the eigenbasis, move singular support away from itself, overcome local pretrace barriers, and create resonances at CM points, unifying upper, lower, and delocalization arguments.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Each use requires different algebraic input; correspondence abundance alone does not automatically supply every lemma or optimal bound.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Eigenfunction size and L-function growth share a convexity barrier
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: General local sup-norm bounds play the role of convexity, while CM evaluation identities translate improved pointwise eigenfunction control into Lindelof-type central-value bounds; Hecke amplification supplies a partial subconvex analogue.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The identities are special to arithmetic eigenfunctions and selected evaluation points, so the analogy is not a general equivalence for all chaotic manifolds.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Trace formulas expose both dynamical and arithmetic nonrigidity
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Positive-dimensional periodic families create trace singularities, while repeated arithmetic lengths create large diagonal mass in a smoothed Selberg trace analysis; both mechanisms force variance lower bounds through different sources of coherent recurrence.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The resulting arguments are lower-bound mechanisms and do not provide the missing upper bounds or unsmoothed control.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Theta lifts are an adversarial boundary for random-wave heuristics
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Gaussian numerical behavior and no-geodesic-scar results do not imply universal random-wave norms: in dimension three, theta-lift subsequences are forced large by arithmetic vanishing even without classical focusing.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exceptional construction is arithmetic and three-dimensional; it does not refute the stated surface conjectures.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmeticity can stabilize or dissolve spectral states through different L-data
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Arithmetic symmetries provide Hecke labels for bound states, whereas under deformation the nonvanishing of Rankin-Selberg values can dissolve cusp forms; spectral persistence is therefore controlled by both operator symmetry and special-value obstructions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The deformation conclusions include simplicity or multiplicity hypotheses and generic statements, not a classification of every surface.

within_source_saturation: Saturated after whole-source inspection: all recoverable nonbibliographic mechanisms, distinctions, theorem/conjecture roles, counterexamples, and proof strategies are represented. Further units would predominantly duplicate the conclusion, isolate routine formulas, promote raw numerical/figure material, or rely on formula-defective OCR without scan verification.
